Steffi Graf. A German tennis champion who won twenty-two Grand Slam singles titles and achieved the Calendar Year Golden Slam in 1988, winning all four majors and Olympic gold in a single year. Her aggressive baseline game and competitive dominance in the late 1980s and early 1990s made her one of tennis's greatest players and most complete champions. She won four Australian Opens, six French Opens, seven Wimbledons, and four US Opens across her career. In 1988 she achieved the Calendar Year Golden Slam, winning all four majors plus Olympic gold, the only player ever to accomplish this historic feat in singles tennis. Known for her powerful baseline game, exceptional footwork, and aggressive forehand, she won titles across all three surface types: hard, clay, and grass. She demonstrated remarkable versatility and skill across the game's different demands. She reached world number one in 1987 and held it for 377 weeks, demonstrating extraordinary consistency. Her peak years from 1987 to 1990 saw her win four consecutive major championships, establishing one of the most impressive runs in tennis history. Her 1988 season is often considered the greatest single season in women's tennis history, an achievement that remains largely unmatched. She retired in 1997 at age twenty-eight while still near her peak, unusual for her era but reflecting the physical and mental toll of her sustained dominance.
